messages.author: 2b446d5b694b4fe0
messages.subject: Ordered probit - alternative specification
parts:
Dear Stan Users!

I am trying to implement an ordered probit model in Stan that is described by John Kruschke (Doing Bayesian Data Analysis, Chapter 23 and briefly here) and written in JAGS (see code attached). The model runs well in JAGS for non-hierarchical models, but crawls for hierarchical problems with larger data sets (e.g. cumulative threshold mixed models incorporating heterogeneous variances/location-scale models, see here or here). 

Diverging from the typical ordered probit model using the unit cumulative normal distribution, and the one presented in section 6.7 of the Stan Manual, Kruschke's model fixes the first and last thresholds/cut-points to constants so that the location and scale of the cumulative normal distribution can be estimated. To do this, a vector of thresholds are supplied in the data list ('thresh' in the model code attached), with the fixed thresholds denoted with constants and the remaining thresholds as NA/missing. 

I have attempted this approach in Stan (see attachment for Stan and JAGS code), but Stan throws an error when missing data is supplied in the threshold vector. I have also attempted fixing the first and last thresholds in the transformed parameters block after declaring the thresholds as parameters, based on another post on this forum where there was code fixing one threshold value, but I receive multiple errors of "accessing element out of range..." and "Error evaluating the log probability at the initial value". 

I am not experienced using Stan, and realise there are likely fundamental issues with my attempted code, so if anyone could offer me a punt in the right direction with writing this model, I'd be really interested! 

Update 22/9/2016: Some mistakes were present in the attached file and by declaring a new ordered vector for the fixed thresholds in the transformed parameters block (and specifying a parameter explicitly for the freely estimated thresholds in the parameters block) means that the model can run and return similar results to JAGS (see newly attached code). 

However, occasionally the value of the freely estimated threshold is lower or higher than the fixed thresholds, meaning I receive warnings at best and, at worst, sampling is not done. Does anyone know how this could be improved?

Update 2: Constraining the threshold free parameter(s) worked (see attached). Obvious when I thought about it...There are still some warnings but the model samples better and faster than JAGS on some other problems, recovering the generating parameter values. 


Thanks
Conor

messages.author: f8a4136bfeaed71c
messages.subject: Re: Ordered probit - alternative specification
parts:
Hi Conor,

I am also running ordinal variable in Stan. As in JAGS, I always allow the cutpoints (thresholds) are unknown and will be estimated from the data. To do that, I think, we should remove the intercept from 'mu'. It means you should remove the 'alpha' from mu[i] <- alpha + beta * x[i]. Actually the number of cutpoints is equal to the number of categories - 1. Then using 'cate-1' cutpoints, then we do not to fix anything. That is what I am doing.

Best,
Tran.

messages.author: 2b446d5b694b4fe0
messages.subject: Re: Ordered probit - alternative specification
parts:
Hi Tran, 

Thanks. The reason I am interested in fixing the first and last thresholds is that, as explained by John Krusckhe (see the original post), is that the mean and sd can be estimated from the data and interpreted on the latent scale. So, rather than estimating different intercepts (1 less than the number of categories) from the data, as is most common in statistical packages, we have one intercept that is the average of the latent scale. I find this much more interpretable, and would like to know if it can be implemented in Stan similar to JAGS. 

I should mention that one user (Oscar Giles) I spoke to off the forum has implemented the Kruschke-style model by algebraically manipulating the Stan manual model to satisfy the different constraints of fixed first and last thresholds (using the functions Kruschke has written about on his blog; see the original post for the link).

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Ordered probit - alternative specification
parts:
If the question is how to create a vector with fixed first
and last position, you can do that with transformed parameters
in Stan a number of different ways. One would be to use
a scaled simplex:


data {
real L;
real<lower = L> U;
int<lower = 3> K; // number of cutpoints
...

transformed data {
real<lower = 0> diff;
diff = U - L;
...

parameters {
simplex[K - 1] cuts_raw;
...

transformed parameters {
ordered[K] cuts;

cuts[1] = L;
cuts[2:K] = L + diff * cumulative_sum(cuts_raw);


- Bob
